title: Residue-compatible pullback and the three-factor local Frobenius operator
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $f_0:W_0\to X_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and $f:W\to X$ its base change to $k$. Use the rational and common-stage constructible categories, Weil pairs and pullback of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Put $G_T=Lg_T^*$ for the geometric-Frobenius automorphism on $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$. These are exact autoequivalences preserving the standard $t$-structures [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], including when $g_T$ is not $k$-linear. For $m\ge1$, let $\alpha_m:G_W^mLf^*\simeq Lf^*G_X^m$ be the comparison induced by $g_X^mf=fg_W^m$ using the rationalized associative integral pullback compositors [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition].

For a Weil complex $(K,\theta)$ set $\theta_f=Lf^*(\theta)\alpha_1$. This defines the induced pullback on Weil pairs, and its iterates satisfy
$$(\theta_f)^{[m]}=Lf^*(\theta^{[m]})\alpha_m.$$
Let $z\in W_0$ and $x=f_0(z)\in X_0$ be closed points such that the actual residue map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism over $k_0$. Put $r=[\kappa(x):k_0]=[\kappa(z):k_0]$. For compatible embeddings of these fields in $k$, take $\bar x=f\bar z$ with common source $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The inverse pullback-composition comparison followed by the point fibre [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] gives a specified natural isomorphism of derived coefficient objects
$$c_K:\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar z^*Lf^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar x^*K.$$
For the three-factor local operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], one has $c_KF_z=F_xc_K$ as an equality of derived morphisms, not merely of traces. The comparison identifies separately the iterated point transports $I^{[r]}$, the return pullback compositors for $g_T^r\bar t=\bar t g_s^r$, and the maps induced by $\theta^{[r]}$. It consequently gives the same intertwining equation on every coefficient cohomology group and the canonical Frobenius-equivariant stalk isomorphism for a constructible sheaf [def-weil-constructible-heart].

If $f_0$ is a locally closed immersion (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]), every closed $z\in W_0$ has closed image and the displayed residue-map hypothesis holds, with both residue fields of size $q^r$ [def-weil-residue-field]. All the comparisons just specified commute with finite coefficient extension and define maps at $\Qlb$. Every finite diagram of Weil objects, arrows, inverse Weil arrows, and equations between their composites can be represented over one finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ after enlargement; the two inverse equations already hold at this stage, and no Frobenius-stable integral lattice is required.

proof.text: For finite coefficients E, use the recorded isomorphismFieldTransport for the scheme automorphism g_T and its inverse, without imposing k-linearity. Its rational and common-stage functors are the actual pullbacks and are inverse equivalences. On an integral representative M in either standard half-category, the exact module inverse image commutes with derived cohomology; the recorded comparison lambda identifies this with constructibleIntegralPullback. Therefore the pulled-back representative has the same cohomological vanishing. The recorded rational object comparison gives the required rational standard-class witness. For common stages, apply this at the representative coefficient field and use the stage comparison. Apply the same argument to the inverse and compose with the recorded counit to obtain reflection of both standard half-categories. For triangulated exactness, take the normalized descended shifts and exactness from automorphismConstructibleStage_descended_shifts. The integral normalization uniquely identifies the ambient shift with fieldIntegralPullShift; faithfulness of the constructible inclusion then identifies the restricted shift with fieldConstructiblePullShift. Rational localization uniqueness identifies the rational shift with fieldRationalPullShift. The common-stage uniqueness, tested on its finite representatives, similarly identifies the common shift with fieldCommonPullShift. Substitution therefore proves exactness for precisely the canonical shifts in the statement, rather than for an arbitrary shift structure.

proof.text:
Write $P_h=Lh^*$ and $d_{h,k}:P_hP_k\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{kh}$ for the inverse of the specified compositor. Use its associativity to identify powers with pullback along powers. Since $f$ is the base change of $f_0$, the two projections of $g_Xf$ and $fg_W$ agree, so these scheme morphisms agree, also for every power. Consequently
$$\alpha_m=d_{f,g_X^m}^{-1}d_{g_W^m,f}:G_W^mP_f\longrightarrow P_fG_X^m.$$
These are natural isomorphisms by [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], rationalized. Set $\theta_f=P_f(\theta)\alpha_1$. For a Weil arrow $u$, naturality gives
$$P_f(u)\theta_f=P_f(u\theta)\alpha_1=P_f(\theta'G_Xu)\alpha_1=\theta'_fG_W(P_fu).$$
Thus $P_f$ on objects and arrows is the claimed functor of Weil pairs; identities and composition are those of $P_f$.

source.place: Restriction paragraph: same stalk and local Frobenius; explicit coherence argument by Q119.

proof.text:
Put $P=P_f$. Associativity of the specified compositors gives, with the power identifications just fixed,
$$\alpha_{m+1,K}=\alpha_{m,G_XK}\,G_W^m(\alpha_{1,K}).$$
Indeed both sides first collapse the word of pullbacks along $g_W^m,g_W,f$ to the pullback along $fg_W^{m+1}=g_X^{m+1}f$ and then expand it in the order $f,g_X^{m+1}$; this is the associativity equation of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] twice, with the middle compositor and inverse cancelled. For $m=1$ the required iterate equation is the definition. If it holds for $m$, naturality of $\alpha_m$ at $\theta:G_XK\to K$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
(\theta_f)^{[m+1]}&=P(\theta^{[m]})\alpha_{m,K}G_W^m(P\theta)G_W^m(\alpha_{1,K})\\
&=P(\theta^{[m]})P(G_X^m\theta)\alpha_{m,G_XK}G_W^m(\alpha_{1,K})\\
&=P(\theta^{[m+1]})\alpha_{m+1,K}.
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the iterates by induction on all $m\ge1$.

proof.text: Now let $z,x$ and the embeddings be as in the statement. Their residue-field isomorphism gives the same finite degree $r$; finiteness follows from [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a). The compatibility of the embeddings gives the equality of scheme morphisms $\bar x=f\bar z$. Each embedding factors through $\mathbf F_{q^r}\subset k$, so the returns in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] use the same $h=g_s^r$: $g_W^r\bar z=\bar z h$ and $g_X^r\bar x=\bar x h$. Put $A=P_{\bar z}P_fK$, $B=P_{\bar x}K$, $e_K=d_{\bar z,f,K}:A\to B$, $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$, and $H=P_h$. Then $c_K=V(e_K)$ is exactly the stipulated natural isomorphism, not a separately chosen stalk identification.

proof.text:
For every derived arrow $v:N\to N'$ on $s$, naturality of the point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] says $V(Lg_s^*v)\iota_N=\iota_{N'}V(v)$. Apply this successively to $v,Lg_s^*v,\ldots,(Lg_s^*)^{r-1}v$ and compose; the intermediate factors cancel by these equalities. Naturality of the compositor identifying $(Lg_s^*)^r$ with $H$ then gives
$$V(Hv)I_N^{[r]}=I_{N'}^{[r]}V(v).$$
In particular, taking $v=e_K$ proves the comparison of the first factors:
$$V(He_K)I_A^{[r]}=I_B^{[r]}c_K.$$
This works for arbitrary derived morphisms, not only maps of a chosen complex.

proof.text:
Let $R_{t,K}:HP_tK\to P_tG_T^rK$ denote the return comparison for $t=\bar z,\bar x$. In the notation of Step 2 it is exactly
$$R_{t,K}=d_{t,g_T^r,K}^{-1}d_{h,t,K}.$$
Associativity gives the middle-factor equation on $s$:
$$e_{G_X^rK}\,P_{\bar z}(\alpha_{r,K})\,R_{\bar z,P_fK}=R_{\bar x,K}\,H(e_K).$$
To check it, multiply on the left by $d_{\bar x,g_X^r,K}$. Expand $\alpha_r$ and $R$ by the two displayed formulas. The associativity equation for $(\bar z,f,g_X^r)$ replaces $d_{\bar x,g_X^r}e_{G_X^rK}P_{\bar z}(d_{f,g_X^r}^{-1})$ by $d_{\bar z,g_X^rf}$. Next use $g_X^rf=fg_W^r$ and associativity for $(\bar z,g_W^r,f)$: it rewrites $d_{\bar z,fg_W^r}P_{\bar z}(d_{g_W^r,f})$ as $d_{g_W^r\bar z,f}(d_{\bar z,g_W^r}P_f)$. Cancel $(d_{\bar z,g_W^r}P_f)^{-1}$. The remaining product is $d_{\bar z h,f}(d_{h,\bar z}P_f)=d_{h,f\bar z}H(d_{\bar z,f})=d_{h,\bar x}H(e_K)$ by associativity for $(h,\bar z,f)$ and the two scheme equalities. This is precisely the right side after multiplication by $d_{\bar x,g_X^r}$. Cancel that isomorphism. Only the cited compositor identities are used; no Cartesianity of the Frobenius square is needed.

proof.text:
Naturality of $e$ at $\theta^{[r]}:G_X^rK\to K$ gives the third-factor equation
$$e_K\,P_{\bar z}P_f(\theta^{[r]})=P_{\bar x}(\theta^{[r]})e_{G_X^rK}.$$
Write $F_z$ as the three factors of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Substitute Step 3, namely $(\theta_f)^{[r]}=P_f(\theta^{[r]})\alpha_r$, into its last factor. Apply the displayed naturality equation, then the middle-factor equation of Step 6, and finally Step 5. Functoriality of $V$ yields explicitly
$$\begin{aligned}
c_KF_z
&=V(P_{\bar x}\theta^{[r]})V(e_{G_X^rK}P_{\bar z}\alpha_r R_{\bar z,P_fK})I_A^{[r]}\\
&=V(P_{\bar x}\theta^{[r]})V(R_{\bar x,K})V(He_K)I_A^{[r]}\\
&=V(P_{\bar x}\theta^{[r]})V(R_{\bar x,K})I_B^{[r]}c_K=F_xc_K.
\end{aligned}$$
This proves equality in the derived coefficient category and identifies each of the three factors separately. The separate rational_point_naturality theorem follows by identifying the specified local compositor with fieldRationalPullComp using its normalization on the literal integral representative. Its inverse natural-transformation square gives the required point naturality. The common-stage comparison is identified with zlPullComp by its normalization on the literal integral representative, then naturality is its inverse natural-transformation square.

proof.text: Apply $H^j$ to the derived intertwining equality: functoriality gives $H^j(c_K)H^j(F_z)=H^j(F_x)H^j(c_K)$ and $H^j(c_K)$ is invertible. For a constructible sheaf $K$, [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact] applies to $f$ and the geometric points, which are $k$-morphisms; their pullbacks preserve the heart and the point complexes are concentrated in degree zero. Its displayed stalk/cohomology identification identifies $H^0(c_K)$ with the canonical pullback stalk isomorphism. Thus that isomorphism is Frobenius-equivariant. Step 1, rather than this $k$-linear theorem, handles the semilinear automorphisms. The common_heart corollary uses the existing zlPull_mem theorem on the heart object (K,hK); its underlying pullback is definitionally Common.pull.

proof.text: A locally closed immersion is surjective on stalks. Apply the proved source lemma Scheme.Hom.isIso_residueFieldMap [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-stalks-residue-field-iso] directly, without factorization. The source theorem Hom.finitePoints_eq_closedPoints identifies closed points with points having finite residue fields over the finite base. Hom.mem_finitePoints_iff_of_isIso transports that property to the image. Choose the actual residue algebra through W0.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap. Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank and D.card_base give cardinality q^r, where r is exactly localClosedPointDegree. Hom.pointNorm_of_isIso gives the same cardinality for the target residue field.

proof.text: All the preceding finite-field constructions commute with $E\subset L$. Use the composition/scalar equation of [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension](1), with exactly its specified canonical families, to transport every $d$, its inverse, $\alpha_m$, $e$ and $R_t$; the inverse equation follows by multiplying the equation by the invertible comparisons. These equations are rationalized from the integral ones. The point-fibre scalar comparison is [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], and the scalar compatibility of $\iota$ is explicitly part (2) of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. Composing this last equation $r$ times and the compositor equation gives compatibility of $I^{[r]}$. Naturality of the pullback/scalar isomorphisms of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] gives compatibility of each map $P_t(\theta^{[r]})$. Thus all three-factor equations, and their cohomology maps, agree under coefficient extension. The identity and tower laws in the cited comparisons make these maps well-defined on the common-stage categories, by their stated representative formula.

proof.text: Finally consider a finite diagram at $\Qlb$. Choose stages for its finitely many underlying objects, its Weil maps and their inverses, and its arrows. The common-stage Hom formula in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] supplies representatives after taking one common finite upper field. Each of the finitely many prescribed relations, the arrow equivariance equations, and the two inverse equations for every Weil map is an equality of common-stage Hom classes. By the definition of that equivalence relation each equality holds after some finite further extension. Take a common upper field for all these finitely many witnesses. At that stage all relations hold simultaneously, including both inverse equations, so the representatives really are Weil objects and Weil arrows. The empty diagram uses $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Step 10 supplies all geometric and fibre comparisons at that same stage. Nothing asks for the rational Weil map or its inverse to preserve an integral lattice; only the underlying objects have integral representatives.
